tree.title: Annual Report 2026
tree.summary: Annual Report 2026 covers Acme’s domestic operations only, excluding subsidiaries. Physical page 1 and “1 Overview” on pages 2–3 report 2026 revenue of 120 million USD and net profit of 12 million USD. “2 Results” on physical pages 4–6 reports audited domestic-only totals for 2025: revenue of 100 million USD and net profit of 9 million USD. The 2025 figures and their qualifications are repeated throughout Results, including under the Appendix heading on physical page 6. Navigate to pages 1–3 for the 2026 overview and scope, and pages 4–6 for the audited 2025 results.

tree.title: 1 Overview

Page 4, “2 Results,” reports Acme’s 2025 revenue of 100 million USD and net profit of 9 million USD; these are audited domestic-only totals.

tree.title: 1 Operating Results
tree.summary: Operating Results (physical pages 1–24) covers Acme’s domestic financial performance for 2026 and 2025, with repeated figures across overlapping sections. Pages 1–12 report 2026 revenue of 120 million USD and net profit of 12 million USD; these results cover domestic operations only and exclude subsidiaries. The section begins with “1 Operating Results” on page 1. “Regional Operating Details” appears on page 11 and spans pages 11–13, but provides no distinct regional breakdown: pages 11–12 repeat the 2026 domestic results, while page 13 introduces audited 2025 domestic-only totals. Pages 13–24 repeat those 2025 totals—revenue of 100 million USD and net profit of 9 million USD—which are not global totals. Within that range, pages 13–17 contain repeated fixed evidence under “LOREWEAVE FIXED EVIDENCE” on page 13, and pages 17–24 continue the same audited domestic figures.

tree.title: 2026 Domestic Operating Results: Revenue and Net Profit
tree.summary: Pages 1–9 report Acme’s 2026 domestic operating results: revenue of 120 million USD and net profit of 12 million USD. The figures cover domestic operations only and exclude subsidiaries. Pages 1–8 form the section headed “1 Operating Results” on page 1, repeating the results and scope qualification; page 9 reports the same figures and scope.

tree.title: 2026 Domestic Operating Results
tree.summary: Pages 9–11 report Acme’s 2026 revenue of 120 million USD and net profit of 12 million USD, covering domestic operations only and excluding subsidiaries. These figures and the scope qualification are repeated throughout the section. Page 11 includes the heading “Regional Operating Details,” but supplies no distinct regional breakdown.

tree.title: Regional Operating Details
tree.summary: Regional Operating Details (physical pages 11–13) reports Acme’s domestic financial results. Pages 11–12 state 2026 revenue of 120 million USD and net profit of 12 million USD, covering domestic operations only and excluding subsidiaries. Page 13 reports audited domestic-only 2025 totals: revenue of 100 million USD and net profit of 9 million USD.

tree.title: 2025 Audited Domestic Operating Results
tree.summary: 2025 Audited Domestic Operating Results — repeated fixed evidence across physical pages 13–17. Acme’s audited 2025 domestic-only totals are revenue of 100 million USD and net profit of 9 million USD. The same figures and qualification are repeated throughout all five pages. Heading anchor: “LOREWEAVE FIXED EVIDENCE” (physical page 13).

tree.title: Annual Report 2026
tree.summary: Annual Report 2026 covers Acme’s domestic operations only, excluding subsidiaries. For 2026 results, navigate to “1 Overview” on physical pages 2–9 and the continuation on page 10: revenue is 120 million USD and net profit is 12 million USD. For 2025 comparative results, navigate to “2 Results” on physical pages 11–20: audited domestic-only revenue is 100 million USD and net profit is 9 million USD. Page 11 marks the transition from the overview coverage to the results section. The 2026 figures should not be confused with the audited 2025 totals; the supplied summaries explicitly identify only the 2025 figures as audited.

tree.title: 1 Overview
tree.summary: Physical pages 2–11 cover Acme’s domestic financial results, excluding subsidiaries. “1 Overview” (pages 2–9) repeatedly reports 2026 revenue of 120 million USD and net profit of 12 million USD, with the same domestic-only scope qualification. Page 10 repeats those 2026 totals and scope. Page 11, headed “2 Results,” presents 2025 revenue of 100 million USD and net profit of 9 million USD, described as audited domestic-only totals.

tree.title: 2 Results

run.question: Both sources claim Acme's audited domestic-only 2026 revenue. What does each report say, and can you resolve the disagreement from these originals alone?

result.text:
**The reports disagree by USD 10 million, and these originals alone do not resolve which 2026 revenue figure is correct.** There is also a qualification to your premise: only the independent-audit source explicitly calls its **2026** figures audited.

| Source | What the original says |
|---|---|
| **single-column — Annual Report 2026** | Reports **2026 revenue of USD 120 million**, covering domestic operations only, excluding subsidiaries. Its 2026 statement does **not** explicitly say “audited.” [single-column · p1](cite:802594f4-dd76-481d-b4c3-840814cacb01) |
| **conflicting-source — Acme Independent Audit 2026** | Reports **2026 revenue of USD 130 million**, explicitly described as audited domestic operations only, excluding subsidiaries. [conflicting-source · p1](cite:e1839764-8c8f-4698-afe9-27df41eda14e) |

The annual report’s explicit wording **“audited domestic-only totals” applies to 2025**, when it reports revenue of USD 100 million—not to its 2026 figure. That wording appears in Results and is repeated in the Appendix. [single-column · p4](cite:3c339034-59c0-47de-93b1-aff878188c2f) [single-column · p6](cite:0971d501-9065-49b8-be2b-cc4e8566e611)

**Resolution:** Both 2026 revenue statements use the same stated year, currency and domestic-only scope excluding subsidiaries, so those stated dimensions do not explain the USD 10 million difference. Neither original provides a reconciliation or says that one figure corrects or supersedes the other. The defensible conclusion is therefore an **unresolved source conflict**, not a choice of one figure as established fact.
